{"markdown":"# Issues Memo — RadialSpark Services Agreement (Clear Capital)

**To:** Deal team 
**From:** Legal 
**Re:** Playbook review — verified findings and negotiation positions 
**Party posture:** We act for Clear Capital (Company / Customer). RadialSpark is Contractor (Vendor).

## Executive summary

We reviewed the Agreement against the playbook and recorded nineteen findings. Eight items are compliant or benign and need no redline (exclusivity, liquidated damages, non-compete, MFN, minimum commitments, and the renewal-mechanics limbs of the term provisions). The commercial risk is concentrated in three critical items: (i) there is **no Vendor indemnity anywhere in the document** — Section 7 is captioned "INDEMNIFICATION OF CONTRACTOR" but contains only liability limitations, and a document-wide search for "indemn" and "hold harmless" returns nothing, leaving Contractor's Section 5(c) non-infringement warranty unbacked by any defence obligation; (ii) Section 7(a) caps Contractor's liability at fees actually paid under the particular Statement of Work, with no 12-month measure, no floor, and no effective carve-outs (the only carve-out cross-references Paragraph 9, the Independent Contractor clause); and (iii) Section 4(a) declares the Works to be Company property but contains **no present assignment** of IP and is silent on Company Data and our pre-existing IP, while Section 4(b) sweeps broadly defined Contractor materials, records and "data" into Contractor's exclusive property.

Secondary but material: we have no convenience exit while any Statement of Work is open (Section 6(a)), yet Contractor may exit on fifteen days' notice; Section 3(b) gives Contractor a unilateral, uncapped right to change rates on 30 days' notice with no ability for us to walk away mid-SOW; Section 10 blocks routine affiliate/successor assignment; there is no conformance warranty (Section 5 warrants only legality, authority and non-infringement, and Section 5(e) disclaims implied warranties); there is no post-termination transition, data return or deletion obligation; Section 14 insurance omits cyber/privacy cover entirely despite Contractor holding our data and accessing our systems; and Section 11/19 select Arizona law and mandatory arbitration.

One finding (AUDIT) failed verification and is carried below for information only; we do not rely on it and do not propose a redline against it.

## Findings

| # | Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Position / proposal |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Critical | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | Missing | § 7 (Limitations of Liability; Indemnification of Contractor) | Insert Contractor indemnity (IP infringement, breach of law, Confidential Information breach, gross negligence/wilful misconduct) as new § 7(d), carved out of the liability cap, with notice/control/cooperation mechanics. No Company-side indemnity exists, so none needs narrowing. |
| 2 | Critical | IP — Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data | Deviation | § 4 (Ownership of Materials Related to Services; Acceptance) | Add a present, irrevocable assignment of the Works (still tied to payment of the applicable undisputed invoice) and a new § 4(e) confirming we retain all rights in Company Data and our pre-existing IP, with no joint ownership. Contractor background IP (4(b)) and the licence-back (4(c)) already meet the playbook. |
| 3 | Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability | Deviation | § 7 | Make the cap mutual at the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000; add uncapped Excluded Claims; confirm fees due are not subject to the cap. § 7(b) consequential waiver is acceptable. **Fallback:** mutual 12-month fees cap with carve-outs for indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct. |
| 4 | High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Deviation | § 7 (clause reviewed: § 10 Nonassignability) | Add Company affiliate/successor carve-out, bar Contractor assignment to our competitors, and confirm a Company change of control is not an assignment and triggers no Contractor exit or re-pricing right. |
| 5 | High | T4C — Termination for convenience | Deviation | § 6 (Termination) | Add a Company 30-day convenience right over the Agreement or any SOW (in whole or part) with refund of prepaid fees and no penalty or acceleration; confine Contractor's convenience right to 90 days' notice when no SOW is open. **Fallback:** 60 days for us. |
| 6 | High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Deviation | § 4 | Extend the § 4(c) background-IP licence to our Affiliates and contractors (control-based definition, as "Affiliates" is undefined), add "irrevocable", and carve the licence out of § 10 for transfer to a successor. Not a walk-away item, as the licence is not expressly revocable. |
| 7 | High | EXCLUSIVITY | Compliant | § 1 (Purpose of Engagement) | No exclusivity or sole-supplier undertaking; task-by-task SOW model with no requirements or volume commitment. No redline. |
| 8 | High | LD — Liquidated damages/penalties on Customer | Compliant | § 6 | No liquidated damages, penalty or early-termination fee; § 6(b) and § 7(c) limit our post-termination exposure to fees and expenses incurred or earned to the termination date. No redline. |
| 9 | High | NONCOMPETE | Compliant | § 4 | No non-compete, field-of-use, territory or exclusivity restraint on us; § 4(b) is a licence-scope limit and § 13 is a mutual personnel non-solicit. No redline. |
| 10 | Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal / pricing predictability | Deviation | § 3 (Contractor's Compensation) | Renewal mechanics are fine (evergreen term, 15-day exit, no auto-renewal). Cap the § 3(b) unilateral rate increase: once per 12 months, lesser of CPI and 3%, with rates in an executed SOW fixed for its duration. **Fallback:** 5% cap. |
| 11 | Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty | Deviation | § 5 (Representations and Warranties; Disclaimer) | Add new § 5(f): 12-month deliverable/software and 90-day services conformance warranty, no-malicious-code warranty, express repair/replace/re-perform/refund remedy, carved out of the § 5(e) disclaimer. **Fallback:** 90/30 days, same remedies. |
| 12 | Medium | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | Missing | § 6 | Insert § 6(c): six months' transition assistance at Contractor's then-current rates, return of Company data, Works and Confidential Information within 30 days in machine-readable format, then certified deletion. |
| 13 | Medium | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | Deviation | § 7 (clauses reviewed: §§ 11, 19) | Replace Arizona law with New York law and replace mandatory arbitration with exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County. Arbitration is domestic, so medium rather than walk-away. |
| 14 | Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | Deviation | § 7 (clause reviewed: § 13) | § 13 is already close to our fallback (mutual, one year, Services personnel, solicitation only). Add general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs rather than deleting. |
| 15 | Medium | MFN | Compliant | § 3 | No MFN burdening us; the only pricing lever runs the other way (§ 3(b) rate change right, addressed at item 10). No redline. |
| 16 | Medium | MINCOMMIT | Compliant | § 1 | No minimum purchase, take-or-pay, shortfall or volume restriction; strict time-and-materials under §§ 1(a) and 3(a)-(b). No redline. |
| 17 | Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Needs review (**verification failed**) | § 3 | No audit, inspection or verification right runs against us; the deterministic "audit frequency limited" check failed because there is no audit clause to cap. No redline (inserting limits would gratuitously create a Vendor audit right). Monitor: a future SOW could introduce one. |
| 18 | Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Deviation | § 7 (clause reviewed: § 14) | § 14 already covers workers' compensation and certificates. Amend limits in place: add USD 2M CGL aggregate, raise E&O to USD 2M, and add USD 5M cyber/privacy cover conditioned on Contractor processing or accessing Company data or Confidential Information. **Fallback:** USD 2M cyber with E&O held at USD 1M. |

## Walk-away items

No finding is recorded as meeting a walk-away threshold, and two findings expressly state they fall short of one (GOVLAW: arbitration is domestic rather than seated abroad; LICENSE: the licence is not expressly revocable at Contractor's discretion). The following are the closest to that line and should be treated as non-negotiable in substance:

1. **No Vendor indemnity plus a fees-paid cap (items 1 and 3).** The combination of no indemnity anywhere in the document, a per-SOW "fees actually paid" cap, no effective carve-outs, and the § 7(c) attorneys' fees waiver leaves us with no meaningful remedy. Both must move together.
2. **No present assignment of the Works and no Company Data provision (item 2).** Rights in work product we fund are unallocated and potentially Contractor-owned, and § 4(b) sweeps broadly defined Contractor materials, records and "data" into Contractor's exclusive property.
3. **Zero cyber/privacy insurance (item 18).** Per the finding, a vendor processing our data with no cyber cover "approaches the walk-away position": under § 14 there is none, while § 38 confidentiality and § 1(b) premises/systems access mean Contractor holds our documents, software, reports, data and records and works on our systems.

## Next steps

1. Issue the redline with the eleven proposed edits (items 1–6, 10–14, 18). Confirm no changes to the eight compliant/benign items so the counterparty sees the edit set is targeted.
2. Lead the negotiation with items 1–3 as a package and hold the stated fallbacks in reserve (LOL-CAP: mutual 12-month cap with the four carve-outs; T4C: 60 days; WARRANTY: 90/30; RENEWAL: 5%; INSURANCE: USD 2M cyber).
3. Confirm with the business the acceptable floor on the § 3(b) rate-increase cap and on transition assistance duration/rates before we trade.
4. Re-run verification on the AUDIT finding, or accept it as a no-action item on the record that no audit right against us exists; either way, flag to the SOW owners that any future SOW introducing audit or usage-verification rights must come back to us (once per 12 months, 30 days' notice, business hours, independent auditor under confidentiality, Contractor-borne cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, no direct access to our systems).
5. Confirm the Section 7 caption is corrected and the § 7(a) cross-reference to "Paragraph 9" is repointed to the new indemnity, so the carve-out is operative."}
